texts.preamble: Thambali Ramaiah vs The State Of Telangana on 13 September, 2023 Author: K. Lakshman Bench: K. Lakshman Hon'Ble Sri Justice K. Lakshman And Hon'Ble Smt. Justice K. Sujana Writ Petition No.15982 Of 2023 Order:
texts.facts: The police filed a pustelathadu weighing petition for cancellation about 33 grams were of bail and the same is seized. Charge sheet was filed and CC is awaited. Conditional bail was PS Gold pustelathadu granted. weighing about 4 tolas Charge sheet was filed and CC is awaited, 447/22 of RGIA PS Sec.392 r/w Attempt to chain Conditional bail was 511 IPC snatching granted. The police filed a petition for cancellation of bail and the same is pending. Out of the said crimes, Crime No.446 of 2022 of RGIA Police Station and Crime No.387 of 2022 of Shamshabad Police Station, Cyberabad were registered against the detenu for the offence punishable under Section - 392 of 2022, while Crime Nos.447 and 432 of 2022 of RGIA Police Thambali Ramaiah vs The State Of Telangana on 13 September, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/56448138/ 2 Station were registered for the offence punishable under Section - 392 read with 511 IPC. In all the said crimes, the detenu was granted bail. However, the police filed applications for cancellation of the bail in Crime Nos.446, 447 and 432 of 2022. On completion of investigation, the Police filed the charge sheets in all the aforesaid crimes and C.C. numbers are awaited. 8. It is mentioned in the impugned detention order dated 16.04.2023 that detenu has been repeatedly indulging the acts of . (1988) 2 SCC 57 . (1988) 1 SCC 296 KL,J & SKS,J goondaism by committing property offences i.e., chain snatchings targeting lone woman in public places causing sever panic and scare among public, especially women-folk under the limits of Cyberabad Police Commissionerate, thus, disturbing peace and tranquility in the area and acted in a manner prejudicial to the maintenance of 'public order' . Thus, considering the involvement of the detenu in series of criminal activities within a span of 1 month, such as chain snatchings in public places and causing hurt to the public in day-light in an organized fashion and upon perusing the entire material placed before the detaining authority including bail petitions and cancellation of bail applications etc., the detaining authority arrived at the subjective satisfaction that free movement of an offender like the detenu is not safe to the society. There is every likely-hood of the detenu committing similar offences. The detenu is a notorious chain snatcher and would indulge in similar offences of threatening, attacking lone woman.
texts.arguments: Mr. Pothamshetti Manoj Kumar, learned counsel for the petitioner, would submit that the impugned detention order was issued without application of mind. The detaining authority did not consider the entire material properly. Therefore, there is no subjective satisfaction by the detaining authority while issuing the impugned detention order. Thus, the detention order is liable to be [LEAKAGE_MASK]. 6. On the other hand, learned Special Government Pleader representing learned Additional Advocate General would submit that the allegations levelled against the detenu are serious and dangerous in nature and he had engaged in unlawful activities of committing property offences i.e., chain snatchings in public places during day time, creating panic and scare among the public in an organized way under the limits of Cyberabad Police Commisionerate. Thus, he is acting in a manner prejudicial to the maintenance of 'public order', thereby disturbing peace and tranquility in the society. Therefore, he is a 'Goonda' as defined in Clause (g) of Section 2 of the Act No.1 of 1986. The detaining authority, considering the entire material available on record and after arriving at the subjective satisfaction only, passed the detention order in order to prevent the detenu from committing similar offences. There is no error in it. He has also placed reliance on the principle laid down by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in Vijay Kumar v. Union of India 1 and Smt. K. Aruna Kumari v. Government of Andhra Pradesh 2. 7. 10. Section - 2 (g) of the Act No.1 of 1986 defines "Goonda", which means a person, who either by himself or as a member of or leader of a gang, habitually commits, or attempts to commit or abets the commission of offences punishable under Chapter XVI or Chapter XVII or Chapter XXII of the IPC. 12. The Hon'ble Supreme Court in Ashok Kumar v. Delhi Administration 3 observed that preventive detention is devised to . (1982) 2 SCC 403 KL,J & SKS,J afford protection to society. The object is not to punish a man for having done something but to intercept before he does it and to prevent him from doing. 13. In Ram Manohar Lohia v. State of Bihar 4, the Apex Court held as under: Thambali Ramaiah vs The State Of Telangana on 13 September, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/56448138/ 3 "...Does the expression "public order" take in every kind of disorder or only some? The answer to this serves to distinguish "public order" from "law and order" because the latter undoubtedly takes in all of them. Public order if disturbed, must lead to public disorder. Every breach of the peace does not lead to public disorder. When two drunkards quarrel and fight there is disorder but not public disorder. They can be dealt with under the powers to maintain law and order but cannot be detained on the ground that they were disturbing public order. Suppose that the two fighters were of rival communities and one of them tried to raise communal passions. The problem is still one of law and order but it raises the apprehension of public disorder. The contravention of law always affects order but before it can be said to affect public order, it must affect the community or the public at large. , "law and order" also comprehends disorders of less gravity than those affecting public order". Law and order represents the largest circle within which is the next circle representing public order and the smallest circle represents security of State. It is then easy to see that an act may affect law and order but not public order just as an act may affect public order but not security of the State." 14. In Vijay Narain Singh v. State of Bihar 5, a three Judge Bench of the Apex Court had an occasion to deal with the expression 'habitually' and held that the expression 'habitually' would mean 'repeatedly' or 'persistently' implying a thread of continuity, stringing together similar repetitive acts, and a single act or omission would not characterize as an act of 'habitual'. The Apex Court was of the opinion that to qualify as a 'habit', a person must have grown accustomed to leading a life of crime, whereby it would be a force of habit, inherent or latent, in an individual with a criminal instinct, with a criminal disposition of mind, that makes him as dangerous to society in general. Article - 21 of KL,J & SKS,J the Constitution of India enshrined the detenu the fundamental right of personal liberty which is precious right enshrined to the citizens as per the Constitution of India.
